name: Installed native apps
plain: A site cannot list your installed apps, except to check its own related app.
meaning: navigator.getInstalledRelatedApps() (Chrome Android 80, Chrome desktop 140 for PWAs) only answers for apps declared in the site manifest related_applications. Custom URL scheme probing is blocked or prompts. Roughly 0 bits for arbitrary apps.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

fields.name: proxy: getInstalledRelatedApps
fields.range: own related apps only, listed in manifest

fields.name: proxy: custom URL scheme
fields.range: Chrome and Safari show a prompt; no silent result

limits.headline: Can't list your installed apps; can only check its own related app
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the site checks for its own app
can: Check if the site's own listed app is installed on Chrome for Android
Check for its own installed web app on desktop Chrome 140
Offer Open in app instead of an install prompt
cannot: List other apps on your phone or computer
Check apps it did not name in its own site file
Probe custom links without a prompt or block
limits.differs: Chrome on Android and recent desktop Chrome can check the site's own app. Safari and Firefox cannot.

story.what_it_is: A site cannot list your apps. It can only check for its own related app.

marketing.name: getInstalledRelatedApps
marketing.pitch: Chrome describes a way for a site to check whether its own related app is installed, so it can skip prompts.

story.for_you: A website cannot see what apps you have. If it has its own app, it may check that one app so it does not nag you to install it again.
story.for_makers: App lists show health, money, religion and more, so they are very sensitive. The web lets a site check only its own listed app. Everything else stays hidden.

use_cases.example: A shop checks whether its own app is installed and hides the Get the app banner if so.
A social site checks for its own app and offers Open in app instead of install.
A music site checks its own app and switches to it when you press play.
An advertiser wanted your whole app list to profile you and cannot get it.
A game site checks its own mobile app to offer cross play sign-in.
A tracker wanted to check for banking or dating apps and cannot.
A bank site checks only its own app to offer a one tap login handoff.

risks: Only works for declared related apps

technical_bounds: App list reveals health, religion, orientation

legit_uses: None: the browser deliberately withholds it
abuse: Sites attempt proxies to recover it
